stu_001: You can recognise it as the lime shading the church garden, where the parish invites people to sit. It stands in front of the Bernhardskirche in Rohracker.
stu_004: You can recognise it as the mulberry standing on Oberdorfplatz, in the old village centre of Möhringen. Look closely at the leaves, glossy if white mulberry, rough as sandpaper if black.
stu_005: You can recognise them by their needles, turning rust orange before dropping in autumn, and by woody knees rising from wet ground around the trunks. They stand in the Kurpark in Bad Cannstatt.
stu_006: You can recognise it by its trunk, forking low into a wide, many-branched crown, standing with two sycamore maples as its company. It stands on the lawn in front of Schloss Solitude.
stu_007: You can recognise it by its trunk, splitting cleanly into two about four metres up. It stands in the Exotic Garden of the Hohenheimer Gärten, at the University of Hohenheim.
